public_summary:
Scene 005: only one real-robot episode was run, using 51 turns; `finish_episode` was called to close it.

Observation: The bottle has been lifted off the table and is nearly upright, with the cap up and base down. It remained in place during a 2-second stationary observation. Final success is for the on-site operator to confirm.

[Recording directory](#/platforms/piper/tasks/lift_bottle/episodes/4ab8a5460c8cb330a716)

The motors remained enabled at the end; logical closure does not confirm physical stopping or a guaranteed holding torque.

manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the bottle on the table and lift it.

Task description: The target is the bottle lying horizontally on the left side of the table. The right arm is available this round. Grasp and lift the bottle off the table, bringing it nearly upright with the cap facing up.

Success criteria: The bottle is held by the gripper and lifted as a whole off the table, with its body nearly vertical, cap up and bottom down. Merely lifting the bottle off the table while it lies horizontally does not count as completion.

## Execution tips

- Prefer gripping the flatter side walls around the middle of the bottle body, with the gripper closing across its long axis. Set the opening slightly wider than the bottle diameter at that point; avoid gripping only the shoulder, cap, or bottom edge, which could slip.
- The fingers partly obscure the bottle in the right camera. Before closing, use the head view to confirm they lie on opposite sides and watch fingertip-to-table clearance to avoid rolling the bottle with one-sided pressure or pressing the table.
- Lift slightly off the table to check whether the bottle slides or rotates between the fingers. If it needs a new grasp, let it rest on the table for support before releasing.
- When adjusting the bottle’s orientation, leave enough clearance below the bottom for it to swing downward. Make small pose adjustments to avoid the bottom brushing the table and causing a drop.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start exactly one real-robot episode with the specified parameters and follow the returned manual and live observations; when finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

The manual and live images confirm the target is the bottle lying on the left, with only the right arm available. I am approaching its middle from above, then will make a small lift to check stability before turning it cap-up.

The gripper is open above the bottle, which remains lying on its side. Next I will use smaller descent steps and align the gripper's closing direction across the bottle, confirming the fingers are on opposite sides before closing.

A steeper downward approach reached the controller's joint limits and returned a recoverable rejection after a small arm movement. I will replan from the returned measured position, reduce tilt, and continue aligning in small steps.
The bottle's middle is aligned between the fingers, and it has not been pushed. I am descending in steps of about 1 cm, checking fingertip clearance from the table each time.
The gripper has begun closing. Its opening feedback is delayed, so I will wait and confirm contact before performing a small test lift.

During the small test lift, the bottle rose with the gripper, remained stable between the fingers, and showed no slipping. I will lift further to allow its bottom to rotate downward, then gradually turn the cap upward.

The bottle is clearly off the table with stable grasp opening and body position. Rotation toward cap-up has begun. After each orientation adjustment, I will check for sliding and bottom-to-table clearance.
The bottle remains stable while adjusting its pose in the air. I also adjusted the wrist orientation to preserve joint range; the body is still tilted and has not yet met the near-upright condition.

The cap is now facing upward and the bottom remains off the table, but the bottle still needs to be made more upright. I am adjusting the wrist based on measured joint angles before completing the final rotation.

The bottle has not slipped, and its cap is visibly higher than its base. To complete the remaining rotation and avoid wrist pose limits, I will lift it a little higher and continue adjusting in small angular increments.

There is enough height to turn the bottle upright, and it remains securely grasped. One wrist rotation had delayed feedback, but a later measurement confirmed it reached the target. I will continue adjusting based on the latest pose.

The bottle body is nearly upright but still tilted slightly forward-back and sideways. Next I will move the grasp point slightly inward, leaving enough joint range for the final adjustment, then hold still and observe.

The bottle remains lifted, with only a small residual tilt. I will make one final small-angle correction and wait to observe stability; whether it meets “nearly vertical” will be confirmed by the on-site operator.
